headline: The US 10 year Treasury yield touched 5.01 percent for the first time since 2023 as a Saudi pipeline shutdown drove WTI to 102 dollars, pushing futures odds of a Fed rate hike on 16 September to roughly 87 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed at 7,619.98, down 0.48 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.56 percent to 26,186.41 after Anthropic's Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk all argued over the weekend for slowing frontier AI development, which sent a semiconductor gauge down 5.9 percent. Money rotated out of the AI buildout chain and into names seen as less dependent on that capital spending, while the 10 year yield briefly breached 5 percent on Friday's hotter August CPI at 0.4 percent month on month and 3.4 percent year on year, and the VIX rose 7.95 percent to 17.10.
summary.india: NSE and BSE were shut on Monday 14 September for Ganesh Chaturthi, so the last print remains Friday's Nifty 50 close of 23,398.10, down 0.34 percent on the day and 2.09 percent on the week, with Bank Nifty at 56,606.55. FIIs sold a net Rs 930.90 crore of cash equities on 11 September against DII buying of Rs 1,968.20 crore, the rupee is at 95.03 to the dollar on the price feed, and GIFT Nifty pointed to a modestly higher reopen with crude, US yields and the Fed decision the dominant inputs.
summary.global: The KOSPI is down 3.14 percent as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix extend losses on the AI spending reassessment, while the Nikkei 225 is off 0.21 percent with a Bank of Japan decision on 18 September and reports pointing to a hike to 1.25 percent. Brent is at 106.48 dollars after Saudi Arabia closed its East to West pipeline following attacks launched from Iraqi territory and a vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, and gold fell 1.54 percent to 4,341.10 dollars as higher rates repriced the metal.

calendar.what: US FOMC meeting begins. India markets reopen after the Ganesh Chaturthi holiday. US Senate procedural vote on the CLARITY Act, 2:15 pm ET.

US FOMC decision 2:00 pm ET with the Summary of Economic Projections and the Chair's press conference; futures put roughly 83 to 89 percent odds on a 25 basis point hike to 4.00 percent. US August retail sales 8:30 am ET, consensus 0.8 percent month on month. NSE IPO anchor book.
Bank of England rate decision 7:00 am ET, consensus unchanged at 3.75 percent. NSE and Sonaselection India IPOs open.

Bank of Japan rate decision; reports cited by 24/7 Wall St. point to a move to 1.25 percent. Hero Motors, SS Retail and Jindal Supreme IPOs close. Holtec Nuclear and Orion180 expected to price on Nasdaq.
NSE and Sonaselection India IPOs close. Meta ex dividend date for its $0.525 payout.
RBI Monetary Policy Committee meeting begins, 5 to 7 October; the repo rate has been held at 5.25 percent for four consecutive reviews.
